trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.location: Generalitat de Catalunya, 6, Sant Just Desvern, ES (41.3772,2.0791)

day_by_day.evening: Arrive at El Prat Airport at 19:20. Take the L9 Sud metro line to Torrassa, then transfer to reach Sant Just Desvern area (approx. 45-60 min, ~€5.15 with T-Casual card). Check in to Sercotel Porta Barcelona. Once settled, take a short stroll around the Sant Just Desvern neighborhood to get your bearings and grab a casual dinner nearby.

meals.lunch: N/A - on the plane or airport
meals.dinner: Bar Restaurant Can Rafel or a local neighbourhood bar in Sant Just Desvern — menú del día (set menu) typically €10-13 even in the evening, includes starter, main, drink, and dessert.

day_by_day.notes: Buy a T-Casual 10-trip metro card at the airport (€11.35) — it will save money throughout the trip. Keep arrival light; you only need to settle in tonight. August heat can be intense even at night (~24°C), so stay hydrated.

day_by_day.morning: Gothic Quarter Walking Tour: Head into central Barcelona via metro (L3 green line from Zona Universitària or bus). Spend the morning on a self-guided or free walking tour of the Gothic Quarter. Explore the Barcelona Cathedral (free entry before 12:30), Plaça Reial, the Roman walls, and the narrow medieval lanes. Free walking tours depart from Plaça de la Catalunya around 10:00 (tip-based, budget €5-10).
day_by_day.afternoon: La Boqueria Market Food Experience: Walk up La Rambla to Mercat de la Boqueria. Browse the stalls, sample fresh fruit juices (€1-2), try a small tapa or jamón ibérico bite. Avoid overpriced stalls at the front — head to the back for better value. Afterwards, explore El Raval neighbourhood and visit the MACBA (Museum of Contemporary Art) plaza, a free outdoor hangout popular with skaters and locals.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Barcelona's famous nightlife on a budget. Start with pre-drinks ('botellón' style) at a convenience store or supermarket near the waterfront. Head to Barceloneta beach area for free sunset views, then explore the bars along Carrer del Parlament in Sant Antoni — lively, local, and affordable. Many bars have €3-4 beers and free entry before midnight.

meals.breakfast: Granja Viader or a local café near the Gothic Quarter — café amb llet (coffee with milk) and a croissant or toast with tomato for €3-5.
meals.lunch: Inside La Boqueria or nearby — fresh fruit, a small bocadillo (sandwich), or a tapa plate for €6-10 total.
meals.dinner: Bar Marsella area or a menú del día restaurant in El Raval — look for set menus around €10-12 including wine.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — the Gothic Quarter has uneven cobblestones. Keep an eye on your belongings on La Rambla, as it is a known pickpocket hotspot. August temperatures peak around 29°C so carry water.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour: Book skip-the-line tickets in advance online (€26-33 with tower access and audio guide — the best budget value for this iconic site). Take the metro L2 or L5 to Sagrada Família station. Arrive early (9:00-10:00) to beat the crowds and the peak afternoon heat. The guided tour lasts approximately 1.5-2 hours. Marvel at Gaudí's extraordinary facades, the forest-like interior, and the stained glass light show.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Sagrada Família, walk or take a short metro ride to explore the Eixample district — Gaudí's urban grid neighbourhood. Visit the exterior of Casa Batlló and Casa Milà (La Pedrera) on Passeig de Gràcia for free (interiors are expensive, but the facades are stunning). Walk down the famous 'Block of Discord' (Manzana de la Discordia) to see three rival Modernista buildings side by side. Rest in the shade at Jardins de la Ciutadella park (free entry).
day_by_day.evening: Head to the El Born neighbourhood for the evening. This trendy area has some of Barcelona's best budget cocktail bars and tapas spots. Visit the Palau de la Música Catalana exterior (free to admire outside). Enjoy the vibrant bar scene on Carrer del Rec and surrounding streets. Many bars offer free entry and affordable drinks until late.

meals.breakfast: Forn de Sant Jaume or any local bakery near the hotel or metro stop — pastry and coffee for €3-4.
meals.lunch: Cervecería Catalana or a nearby menú del día spot in Eixample — set lunch menu €12-14 including bread, starter, main, and drink.
meals.dinner: El Born tapas bar crawl — order patatas bravas (€4), pan con tomate (€2-3), and croquetas (€4-5) across two or three bars for a full meal under €15.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book Sagrada Família tickets at least 2-3 weeks ahead in August — they sell out fast. The afternoon sun on Passeig de Gràcia is intense; bring sunscreen and a hat. Jardins de la Ciutadella is a great free spot to cool down mid-afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Park Güell and Gràcia Neighbourhood: Take the metro to Lesseps or Vallcarca and walk up to Park Güell. The monumental zone requires a ticket (€10, book online in advance), but the surrounding park and viewpoints are free. Arrive at 8:00-9:00 for cooler temperatures and fewer crowds. Enjoy panoramic views over Barcelona from the terrace. Afterwards, wander down into the charming Gràcia neighbourhood — a village-within-a-city feel with independent shops and plazas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Montjuïc Hill on a budget. Take the metro to Paral·lel and then the free funicular (included with metro T-Casual card) up to Montjuïc. Visit the Castell de Montjuïc (€5 entry or free on Sundays after 15:00) for sweeping harbour views. Walk through the Jardins de Laribal (free) and enjoy the greenery. The Fundació Joan Miró is nearby (€14, worth it for art lovers, or skip to stay on budget).
day_by_day.evening: Barceloneta Beach and Port Olímpic nightlife. Head down to the beach for a free sunset swim — the Mediterranean is warm in August. Grab a cold beer from a beach kiosk (€3-4). As night falls, the Port Olímpic area comes alive with clubs and bars. Many venues have free entry before midnight and affordable drink deals. Razzmatazz club (€12-15 entry) is one of Europe's best clubs if you want a full nightlife experience.

meals.breakfast: Grab a fresh juice and pastry from a market stall or café in Gràcia — around €4-5.
meals.lunch: Mercat de l'Abaceria (Mercat de Gràcia) — a local market with affordable food stalls, lunch for €8-10.
meals.dinner: Chiringuito (beach bar) at Barceloneta — grilled fish or paella for €10-14, or a bocadillo and cold drink for €6-8 to keep costs down before a big night out.

day_by_day.notes: Park Güell monumental zone tickets must be booked online in advance. The free areas of the park are still beautiful and worth visiting even without a ticket. Montjuïc is best visited in the late afternoon when temperatures drop slightly. Carry a light layer for the evening sea breeze.

day_by_day.morning: Poblenou and 22@ Innovation District Architecture Walk: Take the metro to Poblenou (L4 yellow line). This up-and-coming neighbourhood blends industrial heritage with cutting-edge contemporary architecture — a hidden gem for architecture lovers. Walk along Rambla del Poblenou (the local, less touristy version of La Rambla), explore street art, and admire the contrast of old factories converted into creative spaces. Visit the free Palo Alto Market if it falls on a weekend.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city centre for last-minute sightseeing and souvenir shopping. Revisit any favourite spots — the Gothic Quarter, Passeig de Gràcia, or El Born. Visit the Palau de la Música Catalana exterior one more time or take a self-guided architecture photo walk. Pick up affordable souvenirs at local shops rather than tourist traps — Mercat de Sant Antoni has great second-hand books and local goods.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner and final night out. Splurge slightly on a sit-down dinner at a well-reviewed local restaurant — many offer excellent value set menus even in the evening. Head to the Raval or Sant Antoni for a final round of Barcelona's legendary bar scene. Enjoy the warm August night, outdoor terraces, and the city's electric atmosphere before heading back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if included, or a local café near the hotel — toast with olive oil and tomato (pa amb tomàquet) and coffee for €4-5.
meals.lunch: Menú del día in Poblenou — a neighbourhood restaurant away from tourist areas will offer better value, around €10-12.
meals.dinner: Slightly splurge farewell dinner — Restaurant Elsa y Fred or similar in El Raval or Eixample, budget €18-22 per person for a full meal with wine.

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if your departure is later in the day. Validate your remaining T-Casual metro trips for the journey back to the airport. The L9 Sud metro line connects directly to the airport terminals — allow 60-75 minutes from the hotel area to the airport including transfers. August 47.5mm monthly rainfall means occasional afternoon thunderstorms are possible — carry a small umbrella.

day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Barcelona El Prat Airport at 19:20. Take the Aerobus or metro L9 Sud to the city, then connect to Sant Just Desvern via taxi or bus to check in at Sercotel Porta Barcelona. Freshen up and take a relaxed stroll around the local neighbourhood to get your bearings.

meals.breakfast: N/A – on board or at airport
meals.dinner: Dinner near the hotel at a local Catalan restaurant such as a neighbourhood 'restaurant del dia' in Sant Just Desvern – try a set menu with pa amb tomàquet, grilled fish or meat, and a glass of house wine for around €15–20 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light – jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Confirm hotel check-in time in advance. The Sercotel Porta Barcelona is in Sant Just Desvern, roughly 10–15 minutes by taxi from central Barcelona. Pick up a T-Casual metro card the next morning to save on transport costs throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour – Head into central Barcelona via metro (L3 or taxi, ~20 min from hotel). Join a skip-the-line guided tour of Gaudí's iconic unfinished basilica. Arrive early (opening time ~09:00) to beat the August crowds and enjoy the morning light streaming through the stained-glass windows. Allow 1.5–2 hours for the full experience including the towers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Park Güell & Gràcia Neighbourhood Exploration – Take a short taxi or bus ride up to Park Güell. Explore the mosaic terraces, gingerbread gatehouses, and the Monumental Zone (book timed entry tickets in advance). Afterwards, wander down into the charming Gràcia neighbourhood – browse its bohemian squares like Plaça del Sol and Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia, pop into independent boutiques, and soak up the local atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to freshen up, then head back into the city for a relaxed evening in the Eixample district. Stroll along Passeig de Gràcia to admire the illuminated facades of Casa Batlló and Casa Milà (La Pedrera) – both stunning at night. Enjoy a pre-dinner vermouth at a classic Eixample bar before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or grab a coffee and croissant at a local café near the hotel before heading out.
meals.lunch: Casual lunch in Gràcia – try a neighbourhood bodega or tapas bar for patatas bravas, croquetas, and pan con tomate. Budget around €12–18 per person.
meals.dinner: Mid-range dinner in Eixample – look for a modern Catalan bistro offering a set evening menu (menú de degustació) for around €25–35 per person. Try dishes like fideuà, escalivada, or grilled Iberian pork.

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família and Park Güell tickets online well in advance – both sell out weeks ahead in August. Wear comfortable shoes; August heat can be intense, so carry water and sunscreen. The Monumental Zone at Park Güell has a timed entry system.

day_by_day.morning: La Boqueria Market Food Experience – Take the metro to Liceu (L3) and dive into Barcelona's legendary public market on La Rambla. Join a guided food experience or explore independently – sample fresh tapas, jamón ibérico, local cheeses, seafood, and tropical fruits. Arrive before 10:00 to avoid the worst of the tourist crowds. Pick up snacks for later.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gothic Quarter Walking Tour – Just steps from La Boqueria, immerse yourself in Barcelona's medieval Gothic Quarter. Join a guided walking tour to discover Roman ruins, the Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, and hidden alleyways with centuries of history. The tour typically lasts 2–2.5 hours. Afterwards, explore independently and browse the antique shops and art galleries in the area.
day_by_day.evening: Barceloneta Beach & El Born Nightlife Circuit – Head to Barceloneta Beach for a golden-hour sunset stroll along the Mediterranean shore (around 20:30–21:00 in August). Grab a refreshing drink at one of the beach chiringuitos. Then migrate into the trendy El Born district for dinner and the start of Barcelona's famous nightlife – explore cocktail bars, live music venues, and buzzing terraces.

meals.breakfast: Eat at La Boqueria itself – fresh fruit, a tortilla española bocadillo, and a café amb llet from one of the market bars. Budget €8–12.
meals.lunch: Light lunch in the Gothic Quarter – a bocadillo or a set lunch menu at a side-street restaurant away from the main tourist drag. Around €12–15 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner in El Born – try a contemporary tapas restaurant such as a pintxos bar or a modern Catalan spot. Budget €20–30 per person. Recommended: grilled octopus, cured meats, and local craft beer or cava.

day_by_day.notes: La Boqueria is extremely crowded mid-morning in August – go early. Many stalls are tourist-oriented; venture to the back of the market for more authentic and better-priced produce. El Born bars typically get lively after 22:00 – pace yourself for a late night if you wish to experience Barcelona's nightlife properly.

day_by_day.morning: Free morning / Architecture Self-Guided Walk – Sleep in slightly to recover from the previous evening. After a leisurely breakfast, take a self-guided architecture walk along Passeig de Gràcia. Visit the 'Block of Discord' (Manzana de la Discordia) featuring Casa Lleó Morera, Casa Amatller, and Casa Batlló. Consider booking a Casa Batlló interior visit (book online) for a truly immersive Modernista experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Montjuïc Hill Exploration – Take the metro to Paral·lel and ride the Funicular de Montjuïc up to the hill. Visit the Fundació Joan Miró (world-class modern art in a stunning rationalist building by Josep Lluís Sert), stroll through the gardens, and enjoy panoramic views over the city and port. If time allows, walk up to the Castell de Montjuïc for sweeping 360° views.
day_by_day.evening: Barceloneta Nightlife & Waterfront – Head back down to the waterfront. Start with dinner in the Barceloneta or Port Olímpic area, then explore the nightlife scene. Barcelona's clubs and beach bars in this area get going after midnight – enjoy cocktails at a rooftop bar or a beachfront club. This is a great night to experience Barcelona's legendary after-dark energy.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a café in Eixample – try a traditional Spanish breakfast of tostada con tomate y aceite with fresh orange juice and coffee. Around €6–9.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Fundació Joan Miró café or a nearby restaurant on Montjuïc with city views. Budget €15–20 per person.
meals.dinner: Seafood dinner in Barceloneta – fresh grilled fish, paella, or fideuà at a mid-range restaurant. Budget €25–35 per person. Avoid the most tourist-facing spots on the beachfront; look for restaurants one block inland for better value.

day_by_day.notes: Casa Batlló tickets are pricey (€35–45) but the interior is extraordinary for architecture lovers – worth it. The Fundació Joan Miró is closed on Mondays, so confirm opening hours. Montjuïc is very exposed to the sun in August – visit in the late afternoon when it's cooler.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed Morning & Last-Minute Exploration – Enjoy a slow breakfast and check out of the hotel (or store luggage). Take a final stroll through whichever neighbourhood resonated most – perhaps a return to El Born for coffee and pastries, or a walk along the Rambla del Poblenou (a quieter, more local version of La Rambla). Browse any remaining souvenir shops or design stores for gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Poblenou & @22 Innovation District Architecture Walk – Explore the up-and-coming Poblenou neighbourhood, Barcelona's former industrial district now transformed into a creative and tech hub. Admire striking contemporary architecture, street art, and design studios. Visit the Rambla del Poblenou, Palo Alto Market (if open on weekends), and the beachfront Parc de la Ciutadella if time allows – a beautiful green oasis with a monumental cascade fountain.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner & Departure Prep – Enjoy a final celebratory dinner in the city before heading back to the hotel or directly to the airport depending on your departure schedule. Choose a restaurant that captures the essence of your trip – perhaps a rooftop terrace with city views or a classic Catalan restaurant for a proper send-off.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or a café stop in El Born – try a croissant de mantequilla and a cortado at a local bakery. Around €5–8.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Poblenou – the neighbourhood has excellent mid-range restaurants and trendy cafés. Try a modern Mediterranean lunch for €15–20 per person.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner – splurge slightly on a quality Catalan restaurant. Consider a tasting menu or à la carte with local wine. Budget €35–50 per person for a memorable final meal.

day_by_day.notes: Check your return flight details and factor in travel time back to El Prat Airport (allow at least 45–60 minutes from central Barcelona, more during peak August traffic). Store luggage at the hotel or at Barcelona Sants station if needed. Poblenou is easily reached via metro L4 (Poblenou or Llacuna stations).

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 19:20
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at El Prat Airport at 19:20. Private transfer arranged to Sercotel Porta Barcelona in Sant Just Desvern (~25 min). Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll around the local neighbourhood to decompress after the flight. Enjoy a relaxed welcome drink at the hotel bar.

meals.dinner: Dinner at a nearby upscale restaurant in Sant Just Desvern — try Restaurante El Celler de Can Roca's sister-style Catalan bistros in the area, or ask the hotel concierge to reserve a table at a premium local spot such as Can Cortada for traditional Catalan cuisine in an elegant 11th-century farmhouse setting.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private airport transfer through the hotel concierge for a seamless arrival. Keep the evening light — no heavy sightseeing on arrival day. Confirm all upcoming tour bookings and restaurant reservations with the concierge tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour: Begin the day with a skip-the-line private guided tour of Gaudí's iconic unfinished basilica. Arrive early (9:00 AM) to beat the August crowds and the midday heat. Marvel at the interplay of light through the stained-glass windows, explore the Nativity and Passion facades, and ascend a tower for panoramic city views. Allow approximately 2 hours for a thorough visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Park Güell & Gràcia Neighborhood Exploration: After a leisurely lunch, head to Park Güell (pre-booked timed entry for the Monumental Zone). Explore Gaudí's whimsical mosaic terraces, the iconic Dragon Stairway, and the Hypostyle Room. Descend into the charming Gràcia neighbourhood — browse its bohemian squares (Plaça del Sol, Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia), pop into independent boutiques, and soak up the village-within-a-city atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to refresh, then head into the city for a premium evening. Enjoy cocktails at a rooftop bar such as the Terraza del Hotel Arts or the Eclipse Bar at the W Barcelona for sweeping Mediterranean sunset views.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café — opt for a full Catalan spread with pa amb tomàquet, cured meats, and fresh pastries.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca — a beloved upscale tapas bar near the Eixample district, perfect between Sagrada Família and Park Güell. Expect premium patatas bravas, croquetas, and fresh seafood montaditos.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Lasarte (3 Michelin stars, Chef Martín Berasategui) in the Eixample — one of Barcelona's finest dining experiences. Book well in advance. Expect avant-garde Basque-Catalan tasting menus with impeccable wine pairings.

day_by_day.notes: August heat peaks in the afternoon (up to 29°C). Schedule outdoor Gaudí sites in the morning and early afternoon. Wear light, breathable clothing and carry water. Book Sagrada Família and Park Güell tickets online well in advance — both sell out weeks ahead in August.

day_by_day.morning: Gothic Quarter Walking Tour: Join a premium private guided walking tour of Barcelona's medieval Gothic Quarter. Discover Roman ruins beneath the city streets, the magnificent Barcelona Cathedral, the ancient Jewish Quarter (El Call), Plaça Reial, and hidden courtyards that most tourists miss. A knowledgeable private guide will bring 2,000 years of history to life. Tour runs approximately 9:30 AM–12:30 PM.
day_by_day.afternoon: La Boqueria Market Food Experience: Stroll up La Rambla to the legendary Mercat de la Boqueria for a curated premium food experience. Sample fresh tapas, jamón ibérico de bellota, artisan cheeses, fresh seafood, and exotic fruits. Consider a private market tour with a local chef who can guide you to the best stalls and hidden gems beyond the tourist-facing counters. Afterwards, explore the nearby El Raval neighbourhood and visit the MACBA (Museum of Contemporary Art) or the CCCB for a cultural afternoon interlude.
day_by_day.evening: Barceloneta Beach & El Born Nightlife Circuit: Begin with a golden-hour stroll along Barceloneta Beach as the sun sets over the Mediterranean. Enjoy a premium cava or Aperol spritz at a beachfront chiringuito. Then transition into the trendy El Born district — start with craft cocktails at El Xampanyet or a speakeasy-style bar, then move to a premium club or live music venue. El Born and nearby Barceloneta are the epicentre of Barcelona's sophisticated nightlife scene.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Federal Café or Nomad Coffee in the Gothic Quarter area — specialty coffee, avocado toast, and fresh-squeezed juices in a stylish setting.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Bar del Pla in El Born — a refined yet relaxed Catalan bistro beloved by locals. Try the croquetes de bacallà, steak tartare, and house vermouth.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Tickets (Albert Adrià's avant-garde tapas bar in Poble Sec) — a world-renowned, playful fine-dining experience. Alternatively, dine at Bodega 1900 (also Adrià) for elevated traditional vermouth-bar cuisine. Reservations are essential and open months in advance.

day_by_day.notes: The Gothic Quarter is best explored on foot — wear comfortable shoes as the cobblestones can be uneven. La Boqueria is extremely crowded mid-morning; aim to arrive by 10:00 AM or after 14:00 for a more relaxed experience. Barcelona nightlife starts late — dinner at 21:00–22:00 is perfectly normal, and clubs don't fill until midnight or later.

day_by_day.morning: Architecture Deep Dive — Modernisme Route: Dedicate the morning to Barcelona's extraordinary Modernisme heritage beyond Gaudí. Visit the Palau de la Música Catalana (UNESCO World Heritage Site) on a guided tour — Lluís Domènech i Montaner's breathtaking concert hall is a riot of stained glass, sculpted columns, and ceramic mosaics. Then walk to the nearby Hospital de Sant Pau, another Domènech i Montaner masterpiece and UNESCO site, for a self-guided exploration of its Art Nouveau pavilions and gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Eixample Architecture Stroll & Luxury Shopping: Spend the afternoon on the elegant Passeig de Gràcia — Barcelona's grandest boulevard and an open-air architecture museum. Admire the 'Block of Discord' featuring Casa Batlló (Gaudí), Casa Amatller (Puig i Cadafalch), and Casa Lleó Morera (Domènech i Montaner) side by side. Enter Casa Batlló for a premium immersive experience (book in advance). Browse the luxury boutiques along Passeig de Gràcia — Hermès, Louis Vuitton, Loewe, and local premium designers are all represented.
day_by_day.evening: Rooftop & Premium Nightlife Experience: Elevate the evening with cocktails at the rooftop of Casa Batlló (if attending a special evening event) or head to the Ohla Barcelona rooftop terrace. Later, experience Barcelona's premium club scene — Opium Barcelona (beachfront, international DJs), Pacha Barcelona, or the exclusive Sutton Club in the uptown Zona Alta are all top-tier options for a luxury nightlife experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Hofmann Pastisseria in the Eixample — one of Barcelona's most celebrated pastry shops, run by the prestigious Hofmann culinary school. Exceptional croissants, ensaïmades, and specialty coffees.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Disfrutar (2 Michelin stars, run by former elBulli chefs) — an extraordinary avant-garde tasting menu experience in the Eixample. One of the most exciting restaurants in the world. Book months ahead.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Moments (2 Michelin stars) in the Mandarin Oriental Barcelona — Chef Carme Ruscalleda's refined Catalan haute cuisine in a supremely elegant setting on Passeig de Gràcia.

day_by_day.notes: Casa Batlló tickets sell out quickly in August — book the premium 'Magic Nights' evening experience for a spectacular after-hours visit with theatrical lighting. Passeig de Gràcia shops typically open 10:00–20:30. The Eixample grid layout makes navigation straightforward. Stay hydrated throughout the day as August temperatures can be intense.

day_by_day.morning: Montjuïc & Pavilion Mies van der Rohe: Take a cable car or private car up to Montjuïc hill for sweeping panoramic views over Barcelona and the Mediterranean. Visit the iconic Barcelona Pavilion (Mies van der Rohe's 1929 masterpiece of modernist architecture — a must for architecture enthusiasts), the Fundació Joan Miró for world-class contemporary art, and stroll through the beautifully landscaped gardens. The elevated position and sea breeze make this the most comfortable outdoor experience on a hot August morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisure, Spa & Farewell Preparation: Return to the hotel for a relaxed afternoon. Indulge in a spa treatment or pool session at the hotel or a nearby luxury spa. Use this time for last-minute souvenir shopping — premium Catalan products such as artisan olive oils, cava, craft gins, and ceramics make excellent gifts. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner & Final Barcelona Night: Celebrate the final evening with a memorable farewell dinner in the city. Afterwards, take one last evening stroll along La Rambla or the waterfront to soak in the atmosphere of Barcelona by night.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at the hotel — enjoy the full spread and take your time before heading out.
meals.lunch: Lunch at La Mar Salada near Barceloneta — a premium seafood restaurant with outstanding paella, fresh grilled fish, and a refined wine list, perfectly positioned near the waterfront for a relaxed final afternoon meal.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at ABaC Restaurant (3 Michelin stars, Chef Jordi Cruz) in the upscale Sarrià-Sant Gervasi neighbourhood — an extraordinary tasting menu showcasing the very best of contemporary Catalan cuisine. A truly unforgettable final evening. Private transfer back to the hotel afterwards.

day_by_day.notes: If departing the following morning, arrange a private airport transfer the night before through the hotel concierge. Montjuïc is best visited in the morning before the heat peaks. The Fundació Joan Miró is closed on Mondays — verify opening hours in advance. Keep the afternoon genuinely relaxed to avoid fatigue before a potential early departure.
